segments.text: I asked my coding agent to give the top bar a bit more room. Two lines of CSS. Then it runs Selfie render. That renders all 142 stories in a pinned container right here on this MacBook Air in under 30 seconds with no cloud and no bill per image. Now it's my turn. The Selfie UI command shows me what changed. Those two lines touched every story, but Selfie has already found the changes repeated across them. I look through them, accept them, and 63 of the 142 are done. But what about dark mode? I search for dark, and there it is, 85,000 changed pixels. Press F and the images swap in place. The top bar went white. Selfie can tell me exactly which pixels changed, but not why. The commit is on GitHub, so I open the same story in the cloud and ask Muse Spark what caused it. It reads the before, the after, the diff, and the code, and it finds the line. Then it spots what I never asked for, a fixed light color where the theme's color used to be. It even tells me to check dark mode. So, back in my review, I click the change, write a note, and send it to the agent, which has been waiting. It gets my words, the exact box, and a picture of what I saw. It puts the theme's color back, renders again, and answers my note. The bar is dark again, and 85,000 changed pixels are down to 13. I approve the rest, and the agent commits and reviews once more. It's the exact same build, so nothing renders. Under half a second and exit zero. Selfie works with any coding agent. If you have a storybook, you can start locally today, and the link's in the description.
